heroHeadline: Iran Peace Offer Rejected — US Official: 'We Will Have Conversation Through Bombs'; Trump: 'Clock Is Ticking'; NSC Situation Room Meeting Tuesday; Saudi Arabia Intercepts 3 Drones — Day 80
heroSubtitle: Day 80 (May 18): Iran's latest revised peace proposal was rejected by a senior US official as insufficient — without concrete enrichment suspension or HEU transfer commitments — prompting the official warning: 'If that's not gonna happen, we will have a conversation through bombs, which will be a shame.' President Trump posted on Truth Social: 'For Iran, the Clock is Ticking, and they better get moving, FAST, or there won't be anything left of them.' Trump is expected to convene his National Security Council in the Situation Room on Tuesday (May 19) to review military options; the Pentagon is reportedly developing a new operational name — 'Sledgehammer' — for a potential resumed campaign. Iran's Ministry of Defence spokesperson declared the military 'fully prepared' to confront any new aggression, while Expediency Council member Mohsen Rezaei warned the US to lift its port blockade or face further confrontation. Saudi Arabia intercepted three drones launched from Iraqi airspace. Global markets fell on escalation fears as Brent crude rose on the 'bombs' threat and continued Hormuz gridlock.
